title: Inventory waste client preflight versus server validation, idempotency, valuation and audit severity
scope: Compare the WinUI waste submission path with API dispatch, RecordWasteHandler, InventoryRules, PurchasingRules, and existing vertical-slice test source. Search lead was unreviewed and absent from the 66 prior semantic group source references; this is one bounded request-path comparison, not repository-wide inventory certification.
decision: No client/server validation divergence was confirmed for reviewed waste quantity, reason, and loss-type contract: client preflights positive quantity and nonblank reason, while server independently validates positive quantity, nonblank reason, and membership in Waste/Spoilage/Breakage before recording. The server is authoritative; UI omits some server-only checks by design. Cost valuation uses latest positive purchase unit cost and persists its result with the movement; missing cost stays null. Critical/warning threshold matches test-source expectations. Existing duplicate-request tests cover sequential and concurrent same-key single-write behavior in the test provider, but no tests were run here. No new canonical finding from this comparison.

behavior.client: SubmitWasteAsync first retries retained payload, then checks parsed quantity > 0 and nonempty reason, obtains inventory_manage approval as needed, and sends loss type, request ID, item, actor and approval. The allowed-type UI selection path is command-gated; client checks are usability preflight.
behavior.server: Handler performs idempotency lookup, parses only enum values accepted by AssertWasteInput (Waste/Spoilage/Breakage), requires positive quantity and nonblank reason, then loads actor/item, authorizes inventory_manage/approval, calculates from latest positive purchase receipt cost, creates one outbound StockMovement and appends audit record before SaveChanges. Unique idempotency key plus conflict reload handles duplicate same-key writes.
behavior.valuation: ValueStockLoss uses latest positive actual purchase unit cost; cost is captured at posting, and absence of a qualifying purchase remains null rather than fabricated zero. The test source documents balance may go negative to preserve real-versus-recorded discrepancy capture.
behavior.severity: Handler assigns critical when quantity >= 10,000 milli-units; existing tests expect critical at threshold and warning below it.

counterevidence_and_limits.security: The handler idempotency lookup occurs before its actor authorization call. The route delegates to this handler; this comparison did not establish all endpoint-level authorization middleware or whether unauthenticated callers can reach it. Treat replay-before-authorization as a security review lead requiring the dedicated Security phase, not as a confirmed bypass here.
counterevidence_and_limits.idempotency: Tests assert same-key sequential and concurrent requests create exactly one movement under the test host/provider, but payload-conflict behavior for reusing one RequestId with different item/quantity was not tested or adjudicated. No SQL Server concurrency behavior is proven.
counterevidence_and_limits.business_policy: Allowing stock to become negative is explicitly documented and supported by test source; do not change without owner requirement. No maximum waste quantity was found or assumed.
counterevidence_and_limits.tests: Existing tests were inspected only; none executed. No database/runtime/financial operation performed.

recommendation: Keep authoritative enum, positive-quantity, reason, and inventory_manage checks at the server/domain boundary even when WinUI preflights them. Preserve latest-purchase frozen-cost and null unknown-cost semantics unless owner approves a costing-policy change. In the separate Security review, determine whether the route has a required authenticated principal before the handler replay branch, and verify replay authorization/data disclosure. Define whether reusing one RequestId with a different payload must be rejected; if so, persist/compare a request fingerprint.
required_tests: API/domain tests reject zero/negative quantity, blank reason, and each non-loss movement enum before movement/audit writes.
Each loss type remains accepted with positive quantity; client still blocks malformed quantity/reason and retains retry payload after uncertain response.
No purchase history yields null unit/loss value; latest positive purchase receipt determines frozen unit/loss value.
Same RequestId same payload sequential and concurrent requests create exactly one movement and return consistent replay result against deployed SQL Server.
Reusing same RequestId with different item/quantity either rejects by documented contract or explicitly returns original immutable result; assert no second write.
Authorization middleware plus handler replay path does not disclose movement/item/loss details to an unauthorized principal.
10,000 milli-units remains critical and values below threshold warning.
related_findings: Existing inventory/idempotency findings should be cross-checked; no new ID created in this comparison.
limitations: Static source plus test-source comparison only; no integration tests executed. Test source indicates test-host sequential/concurrent same-key coverage but does not establish deployed SQL Server isolation/unique-key behavior. Security reachability of preauthorization replay requires full endpoint pipeline review. RequestId payload binding and owner-defined upper quantity policy remain unresolved.

source_references.evidence: Client retained-request path retries pending payload, validates parsed quantity > 0 and required reason, resolves inventory_manage approval, constructs RecordWasteRequest, sends through API and refreshes after success. UI types are selected through gated commands; it is not authoritative.
Request/result shape carries RequestId, item ID, milli-unit quantity, loss type, reason, actor and optional approval; no separate client contract enforces an upper quantity.
POST route delegates request to RecordWasteHandler and maps domain/conflict/not-found errors.

Server replay lookup, loss-type parse, domain validation, actor/item lookup, authorization, latest purchase retrieval, valuation, outbound movement and audit write in SaveChanges; concurrency/idempotency relies on unique key plus conflict reload.

Authoritative allowed loss types and positive quantity/nonempty reason rules; stock balance sums signed directions and does not impose nonnegative balance, consistent with discrepancy recording intent.
Loss valuation freezes latest positive actual purchase cost and returns unknown/null absent qualifying cost; no later recalc of historical movement.

Existing tests assert latest-purchase valuation, unknown cost, invalid loss type, duplicate/concurrent same RequestId single-write behavior, negative stock allowance, and critical/warning threshold. Inspected, not executed.
